scoring_justification: Cannot recompute frequencies from raw artifact because the raw artifact itself is the computed frequencies; we verify that the frequencies fall within physically plausible ranges and the key Fröhlich LO‑TO inversion property holds, which constitutes the paper's main verifiable claim.

outputs.description: Table of computed Fröhlich frequencies; rows correspond to different values of the axial depolarization factor L∥.

output_contract.notes: Absolute frequencies are compared to a hidden reference implementation with tolerance; a structural trend check of the effective-medium model is also performed.

steps.description: LO‑TO inversion for extreme L_parallel values

hidden_assets.purpose: Frequency range thresholds derived from bulk 4H‑SiC phonon frequencies (Harima et al., 1995)
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Bulk 4H‑SiC TO/LO frequencies from Harima et al. (1995): axial TO=783, LO=964; planar TO=798, LO=966.4, with a ±2 cm⁻¹ margin to accommodate small porosity‑induced shifts.
hidden_assets.generation_method: The bulk frequencies ±2 cm⁻¹ produce the bounds. These bounds are physically grounded and any correct implementation of the Maxwell Garnett model with 12% porosity will produce frequencies within these ranges.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The numbers are directly derived from the published bulk phonon frequencies and the allowed shift is based on known experimental and theoretical values for porous SiC.
